newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks rebound to strong midday close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks rebound to strong midday close.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed the Wednesday morning session with good gains, retracing much of Tuesday's slide and confounding brokers' expectations of a short-term pullback in line with overseas markets.
"This market is difficult to figure out," said the head of sales at one local brokerage house. "All I can say is that there is very little selling interest."
The Hang Seng Index put on 64.53 points to close the session at 11,611.23, after trending as much as 106 points higher.
Turnover was a respectable HK$3.0 billion, in line with Tuesday morning after excluding two large share placements.
Brokers said turnover was spread quite evenly through blue chips and second liners. Both mid-caps and H shares were actively traded on Wednesday, they said.
The commercial and industrial sector led the market through the morning, followed by property stocks.

Red chip hong CITIC Pacific rose HK$0.30 to end the session at HK$34.60, after touching a high of HK$34.90. Swire Pacific ended unchanged at HK$68.00, while subsidiary Cathay Pacific grabbed a HK$0.05 gain to HK$12.80 on its 50th anniversary.
Cheung Kong and SHK Properties led the property sector with gains of HK$0.75 each to HK$56.50 and HK$79.25 respectively.
HSBC was unchanged at HK$141.50, and Hang Seng Bank put on HK$0.50 to HK$79.25.

In the mid-cap sector, China Resources added HK$0.25 to HK$7.30. Hong Kong Ferry slid HK$0.45 to HK$13.85 after saying it expected to receive government approval to redevelop its shipyard at Tai Kok Tsui.
Among the H shares, Chengdu Telecom put on HK$0.05 to HK$0.79 on low turnover of HK$759,980.
Newcomer Kwoon Chung Bus Holdings opened at HK$2.30 and ended the morning at HK$2.40, well above the share's offer price of HK$1.80. --Kathleen Kearney (852) 2843 6933
